subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance / SLO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@fintechco.com>, Priya Agarwal <priya.agarwal@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance / SLO recap & next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our demo and the performance / SLO items we discussed so we have an actionable MAP (mutual action plan):

Key SLO items noted during demo:
- P99 latency target: 200ms (api time-to-first-byte for non-streaming; for streaming: time-to-first-chunk <100ms)
- Median latency target: <50ms
- Throughput: steady-state 800 req/min with 2x burst to 1,600 req/min for short windows
- Concurrency: sustained 40 concurrent streams/requests, 60 peak
- Streaming: progressive responses required (server-sent events or chunked HTTP; client shows partial results as they arrive)
- Max response size: typically <2,000 tokens; average ~300 tokens

Attached: redwood-slo-checklist.pdf (checklist + recommended config), sample-benchmark-results.csv (representative numbers from a similar payments workload).

Next steps I proposed in the demo: 
1) Confirm SLO targets above (you + engineering).
2) Provide a representative test dataset and expected traffic profile (Priya / eng).
3) Redwood to propose two options: hosted with routing + caching and a Dedicated reserved pool — include rough capacity and cost delta.
4) 7-day smoke test (POC) on agreed config — aim to schedule for mid-July.
5) Security & compliance kickoff (SOC 2 evidence) — Monica to lead.

Can you confirm the targets above or flag anything we've missed? If those look right, I’ll draft the MAP with timelines and get Rishi/Monica plugged into the technical kickoff.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@fintechco.com>

Cc: Priya Agarwal <priya.agarwal@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance / SLO recap & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side after we synced with engineering for 30 minutes: 

- Baseline: our current internal microservice that does similar inference sits at p99 ~350ms for the workloads we demoed. Getting to p99 200ms is aspirational but would be ideal. Is that p99 number assuming token-level batching/caching?
- Throughput: we should plan for 1,200 req/min sustained during business hours and up to 2,000 req/min for short bursts tied to payroll cycles. Can you confirm if the dedicated pool option supports that footprint with headroom?
- Concurrency: 60 sustained would be better than 40; we expect concurrent sessions during peak to be high.
- Streaming: yes, progressive streaming is a hard requirement — customers expect partial results as they type. We use a WebSocket-based client in our UI today; support for chunked responses or WebSocket would work. Time-to-first-chunk <100ms is important.
- Regional deployment: must be available in us-east (primary) and fall back to us-west. Latency differences between regions will matter.

Also: procurement timeline — we usually need a PO to run dedicated capacity POCs. We’ll likely need a cost estimate and a short statement of work to push to procurement. SOC 2 evidence is required before prod.

Looping in Priya to confirm traffic patterns and to share a lightweight test dataset.

—Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
jordan.smith@fintechco.com

Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance / SLO recap & next steps

Jordan — great questions. Short answers up front, followed by proposed config and MAP items.

1) P99 200ms feasibility
- Short answer: achievable with a Dedicated pool sized for your peak concurrency + our adaptive batching disabled for tail-latency-sensitive routes, combined with KV prefix caching for common prefixes. The hosted option can hit ~250–300ms p99 for similar workloads; dedicated racks with optimized quantized runtimes can reach ~180–220ms depending on sequence length distribution.

2) Throughput & concurrency
- We can support 1,200–2,000 req/min with a Dedicated reserved pool (N GPUs, autoscale buffer). For planning, we recommend sizing for 1,500 req/min sustained with 2x burst policy. Concurrency: recommend planning for 60 sustained; we’ll size to 80 peak to give headroom.

3) Streaming support
- We support chunked HTTP streaming (Time-to-first-chunk <100ms in dedicated setups) and WebSocket for long-lived sessions. For your WebSocket client we’ll provide an integration guide.

4) Region & failover
- We can route primary traffic to us-east and fail over to us-west. We’ll include cross-region warm standby in the SOW if you want <1s failover for active sessions (this is more complex for streaming; typically we recommend session-level fallback to a short-lived stateless endpoint).

Proposed options (docs attached):
A) Hosted (fastest onboard): routing policy, prefix caching, autoscale — target p99 ~250–300ms, lower cost to start, easier to evaluate.
B) Dedicated (recommended for strict p99 & compliance): reserved GPU pool, tuned quantized model, 7-day POC on your traffic — target p99 ~180–220ms, supports required throughput and streaming SLAs.

Rough MAP / next steps (I’ll draft a formal timeline once you confirm option B vs A):
- Today: Confirm SLO targets and traffic profile (Jordan / Priya) — due Mon 7/5
- Tue 7/6: Redwood sends SOW + cost estimate for 7-day POC (Rishi)
- Wed 7/7: Procurement review; we provide PO template + DocuSign (if needed)
- Week of 7/12: 7-day POC kickoff (tech/monitoring links, test dataset ingestion)
- Week of 7/19: Post-POC review and decision criteria evaluation

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (options & rough cost bands). I’ll add a short appendix with model recommendations once I have your average sequence length and exact token budget.

Can you confirm: option B (Dedicated) preferred? And please have Priya drop the representative traffic profile and a small test dataset to the Drive link I shared.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — this looks good. We had a quick exec + procurement sync this morning and the direction is: start with a 7-day Dedicated POC (option B) to validate p99 and streaming behavior. Action items from our side: 

- Priya will upload a representative test dataset and the traffic profile to the Drive link by EOD Monday 7/5.
- I’ll ask procurement to prepare a PO template and aim to send it to you by 7/9. Expect a short SOW + cost estimate from Rishi early next week.
- Security: we need the SOC 2 supporting evidence and a contact for security questionnaire (Monica, looping in your team).
- We prefer us-east primary with us-west failover.

If Redwood can provide an integration guide for WebSocket streaming and a short checklist of the monitoring hooks (latency p99, time-to-first-chunk, token consumption per request) that would help our SREs validate during the POC.

We’re aligned on the decision criteria (p99 <=220ms, time-to-first-chunk <100ms, throughput >=1,200 req/min sustained). If the POC meets those thresholds we’ll move to a reserved capacity contract.

Thanks — will confirm once the PO is in flight.

—Jordan
